summary.short: The Planning and Infrastructure Act 2025 changes UK rules on nationally significant infrastructure consent, electricity connections and benefits, transport and harbour orders, EV charge point accessibility, and English planning fees and decisions, with some provisions applying only in Scotland or Wales.
summary.long: Dated 18 December 2025, this Act amends the Planning Act 2008 to change national policy statement review duties, remove pre-application consultation duties, and let the Secretary of State disapply development consent by direction. It allows electricity licence and connection-agreement modifications for three years, requires the Independent System Operator and Planner and electricity distributors to have regard to designated strategic plans, and directs the Authority to run a long duration electricity storage scheme. It enables regulations for benefits to homes near new transmission infrastructure, with pass-through to end-users, civil enforcement, monetary penalties and information disclosure. It amends the Electricity Act 1989 for Scottish consent procedures, the Highways Act 1980 and Transport and Works Act 1992 (deadlines, fees, deemed consents, publication), and the Automated and Electric Vehicles Act 2018 (charge point accessibility). For English planning authorities it lets fees be set locally within cost limits, allows Secretary of State review directions, permits a planning fee surcharge, requires certified training for relevant members, sets delegation and committee rules, and extends implementation periods after legal challenges. Natural England may decline certain non-ministerial advice requests. Scottish and Welsh provisions apply to their own ministers.

notes: This file covers part 1 of 3: ss. 1–57 (Part 1 Chapters 1–3 and Part 2 Chapter 1 to s. 57). Relations are those stated in this part only; amendments made by later parts are not included. No commencement dates or commencement regulations appear in this part, and the registry status is partially_in_force. Several provisions confer regulation-making or direction powers (e.g. ss. 14, 17, 25, 30, 35B) and are recorded here only where they amend or cite another instrument. No internal inconsistency was identified in this part. Where an instrument is amended, the target_instrument_id is empty because registry IDs were not supplied. Part-of record: covers s. 58 to s. 118(3) and the opening words of s. 118(4), which is cut off at the part boundary and not coded. target_instrument_id is left empty because no registry IDs were supplied; target_text gives the citation. Several amendments (for example to the Habitats Regulations 2017 and the Acquisition of Land Act 1981) are carried out by Schedules whose text is in other parts; relations here rest on the operative sections in this part. No internal inconsistency was identified in this part. This part covers the commencement provisions (subsections (5) to (8), sections 115 to 119 including the short title) and Schedules 1 to 5 (minor, consequential and Part 3-related amendments). Relations are recorded only for instruments amended, applied or referred to here; the amendments themselves are not coded as obligations or thresholds. target_instrument_id is an empty string where no registry ID is known, because the schema requires a string. The section number of the commencement provision containing subsection (5) is not shown in this extract. Schedule 5 para 43 ends with an unfinished insertion '(b) ' with no text, so the amendment to section 100ZA(6) is incomplete on the face of the document.
